A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QRPO work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite additions and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix M report original chat and LeetCode experiments, including baseline comparisons, pre-computation scaling and length-bias analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds an offline-versus-mixed-online training experiment in Appendix A and an empirical quantile distribution in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The quantile transformation, pointwise squared loss, analytic partition function, Algorithm 1 and reference implementation are unchanged. Online training was already permitted and discussed in v1; the new experiment does not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Reported coverage remains general chat using Magpie-Air and UltraFeedback, AlpacaEval evaluation, and LeetCode coding. The new online-training ablation reuses Magpie-Air; no additional dataset, domain or task is reported.

E2.justification: DPO, REBEL, SimPO and the existing initial-model/SFT controls remain in the corresponding benchmark comparisons. Newly discussed methods such as SPO, AGRO and TBA are cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix A adds a comparison between offline-only training and training with mixed offline and online completions, plotting test rewards against training steps. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; the new mixture ratio and sampling schedule are not specified.

E4.justification: V2 adds the online-data ablation in Figure 7 and an empirical illustration of quantile-reward uniformity in Figure 8. It removes Section 3's preliminary log-quantile performance observation. Existing scaling, length-bias and probability-dynamics analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The three repeated evaluation samplings, mean/standard-deviation reporting and AlpacaEval standard errors are retained, including the distinction from repeated training runs. The added figures supply no new run-count or uncertainty information. Appendix C's concentration bounds are theoretical additions.

E6.justification: Benchmark Tables 2–3 and detailed Tables 12–16 retain their scores. V2 newly reports 26% greater reward improvement with mixed online/offline training and adds the empirical quantile histogram. V1's qualitative finding that log-quantile rewards slightly reduce performance is removed.

T1.justification: New Appendix C adds calibration-error and concentration bounds, population-risk invariance under quantile noise, a gradient-perturbation bound and conditional SGD convergence arguments. This substantially extends the existing distribution, variance and asymptotic analyses, which are retained under renumbered appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, numbered contributions and main conclusion retain the same claims: pointwise policy fitting with tractable partition functions, pre-computation scaling, strong chat/coding performance and reduced length bias.

C2.justification: Section 3 replaces its explicit approximate Best-of-N interpretation with a win-rate and inference-aware interpretation. Section 6 replaces the warning that reward reshaping may be suboptimal with acknowledgement that transformations were not empirically explored. Appendix A adds discussion defending KL regularization.

D1.justification: Table 15 newly discloses skipped QRPO off-policy-random configurations, explaining unchanged step-0 entries. The added checklist also states that augmented synthetic datasets are open-sourced with the code. Existing implementation, hardware and hyperparameter descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning through InfAlign, SPO, AGRO, TBA, ReMix and literature on online training and KL regularization. These additions clarify nearby approaches and alternative partition-function estimators while preserving the paper's central positioning.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites Section 3 and the limitations discussion, inserts Appendix C, renumbers subsequent appendices and adds a NeurIPS checklist. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the training-curve comparison and quantile histogram as Figures 7–8, expands Table 15's caption and shifts later appendix material. Existing plot images and table structures are retained; subsequent figure renumbering does not represent new results.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful concentration and risk-invariance analysis, initial evidence for online-data training, and clearer research context and configuration disclosure. These modestly strengthen support for the unchanged method. The gains are limited by sparse settings and uncertainty reporting for the new experiment, and a local sign error in Appendix C.3's gradient-difference identity.
